--- title: Assignment 3 --- This assignment will use the same data that you will use in the [retail project](Project.qmd) later in the semester. Each student will use a different time series, selected using their student ID number as follows. ```r library(fpp3) get_my_data <- function(student_id) { set.seed(student_id) all_data <- readr::read_rds("https://bit.ly/monashretaildata") while (TRUE) { retail <- filter(all_data, `Series ID` == sample(`Series ID`, 1)) if (!any(is.na(fill_gaps(retail)$Turnover))) return(retail) } } # Replace the argument with your student ID retail <- get_my_data(12345678) ``` Use a training set up to and including 2018. - What transformations (Box-Cox and/or differencing) would be required to make the data stationary? You should use a unit-root test as part of the discussion. [2 marks] - Use a plot of the ACF and PACF of the (possibly differenced) data to determine two plausible ARIMA models for this data set. [3 marks] - Fit both models, along with an automatically chosen model, and produce forecasts for 2019--2022. [2 marks] - Which model is best based on AIC? Which model is best based on the test set RMSE? Which do you think is best to use for future forecasts? Why? [3 marks] - Check the residuals from your preferred model, using an ACF plot and a Ljung-Box test. Do the residuals appear to be white noise? [2 marks] Submit a Quarto (`qmd`) file which carries out the above analysis. You need to submit one file which implements all steps above. You may use this file as a starting point. To receive full marks, the `qmd` file must render without errors. Marks will be deducted for files that do not render.
